data.name: RunCommandAction_Description
data.value: Runs a PowerShell or Command Prompt command and gives back what it printed. For advanced users: a command can change or delete anything your account can, so only run commands you trust.

data.name: RunCommandAction_Param_FailOnError_Label
data.value: Stop the shortcut if the command fails

data.name: RunCommandAction_Param_AllowEmpty_Label
data.value: Allow empty variables in the command

data.name: RunCommandAction_Param_AllowPatterns_Label
data.value: Allow wildcards and relative paths in variables

data.name: RunCommandAction_Error_0_Comes_From_A_Step
data.value: {0} comes from a step whose output is private, and private values are never put into a command, where other programs could read them. So the command wasn't run.

data.name: RunCommandAction_Error_0_Is_Empty_So_The
data.value: {0} is empty, so the command wasn't run. Turn on "Allow empty variables in the command" if that is expected.

data.name: RunCommandAction_Error_0_Is_1_Which_Could
data.value: {0} is '{1}', which could point to a different folder or to many files, so the command wasn't run. Turn on "Allow wildcards and relative paths in variables" if that is expected.

data.name: RunCommandAction_Error_0_Contains_A_Line_Break
data.value: {0} contains a line break or one of & | < > ^ % ! ", which Command Prompt could run as part of the command, so the command wasn't run. Choose PowerShell under "Run in" for values like this.

data.name: RunCommandAction_Error_0_Contains_Which_Cmd
data.value: {0} contains '/', which cmd can read as a switch. Use PowerShell for this value.

data.name: RunCommandAction_Error_0_Starts_With_Which
data.value: {0} starts with '-', which a command could read as an option. Use PowerShell for this value.

data.name: RunCommandAction_Error_0_Contains_A_Space_Or
data.value: {0} contains a space or one of ( ) , ; =, which Command Prompt would split or act on, so the command wasn't run.

data.name: QuotedRegion_Error_Type_The_Command_To_Run
data.value: Type the command to run first.

data.name: QuotedRegion_Error_The_Command_And_Its_Values
data.value: The command and its values are too long to hand to PowerShell. Save long text to a file first and pass the file's path.

data.name: QuotedRegion_Error_Couldn_T_Find_The_Folder_0
data.value: Couldn't find the folder '{0}'. Check it exists, or leave it empty.

data.name: QuotedRegion_Error_The_Command_Was_Still_Running
data.value: The command was still running after {0} seconds, so it was stopped. Raise the time limit if it needs longer.

Optionally force it to stop if it hasn't closed in time (unsaved work is lost); forcing only stops that exact program, never Windows itself or programs it started. Gives back true when the app is no longer running.

data.value: Pauses the shortcut until something is true, checking again every few seconds: a time of day, a file or folder appearing or disappearing, an app running or not, the PC being idle, text on the clipboard, or a website answering. It only looks, it never changes anything. If the time limit runs out, the shortcut carries on or stops with a message, as you choose. A time of day that has already passed today means that time tomorrow. Stop running shortcuts ends the wait at once.
